Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right lower lung, to the follow-up image (Figure 4), there is clear progression with increased density in the right lung and the appearance of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of worsening bilateral airspace disease over time is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can present as progressive multifocal consolidation.
